title: Live chunk introspection telemetry and redaction workbench
creator: Priya Raman
body:
Summary:
We need a developer-facing workbench and runtime changes to capture per-chunk telemetry, stitch chunk-level spans into request-level traces, and apply privacy-aware redaction to streamed output while preserving observability for debugging and cost attribution. The goal is a drop-in experience for current streaming APIs but with a compatibility shim that emits v1-style frames and a new v2 introspection frame for internal tools.

Background and motivation:
- Customers ask for finer-grained cost/latency breakdowns for streaming responses (per-chunk token counts, GPU-tokens, decode-latency).
- Debugging streaming failures is hard because traces are either too coarse (single request span) or disclose PII when chunks are logged.
- We must ship a privacy-first telemetry pipeline that supports sampled raw chunks for debugging but otherwise stores only redacted provenance and metrics.
- Several older SDKs expect the legacy stream frame wire format; we need a compatibility layer rather than breaking clients.

Scope and deliverables:
1) Runtime instrumentation: emit per-chunk metrics (token_count, decode_ms, kvcache_misses, batch_id) as structured metrics and expose them to the Console. Metrics will be emitted with chunk_id and request_id tags for correlation.
2) Tracing: implement span stitching algorithm (span-stitch-v2) that creates lightweight chunk spans and attaches canonical request root. Spans must include non-sensitive attributes (duration_ms, gpu_id, model_variant). Raw chunk text must never be placed in span attributes.
3) Redaction pipeline: implement two-stage redaction: (a) fast regex-based scrub for obvious PII at the runtime edge and (b) optional async ML-based scrub for sampled chunks. Provide redaction metadata (redaction_level, scrub_rules_version) in chunk introspection frames.
4) Compatibility shim: provide a v1-to-v2 mapping that allows older SDKs to receive legacy frames while internal tooling consumes richer v2 introspection frames (chunk provenance + redaction metadata).
5) Workbench UI + Playbook: lightweight Console page for live session introspection (stream timeline, per-chunk metrics, trace links, redaction summary) and an internal runbook describing how to escalate sampled raw chunks safely.

Acceptance criteria:
- Per-chunk metrics appear in Console per-session and can be queried by request_id. Examples: sum(chunk_token_count) by request_id, histogram(decode_ms) by chunk.
- Traces emitted for streaming requests show stitched child spans per chunk with stable chunk_id and link to request root. No raw content elements in span attributes.
- Redaction metadata accompanies every chunk; full raw chunks are only persisted for sampled sessions gated by a single-tenant approval flag.
- Backward-compat compatibility shim returns legacy frame envelope for clients indicating wire-version:1; no changes required by legacy SDKs.
- End-to-end tests cover: redaction rule updates, regex edge-cases, ML-scan acceptance sampling, and trace stitching under high concurrency.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- We prefer regex-first at the edge to keep latency low. ML-based scrub runs async and relies on an opt-in sampling policy to limit costs and retention. Trade-off: some subtle PII may slip past regex and require async remediation via ML-scan and customer notification flow.
- Storing per-chunk raw text is high-risk; implement short TTL (default 7 days) and KMS-wrapped storage with ACLs for internal tools only. We'll need legal sign-off for retention window.
- Emitting chunk-level metrics increases cardinality; use aggregation knobs and retention-tiering (hot: 30d, cold: 90d) to control cost.

Instrumentation design (high level):
- chunk_id: uuid
- request_id: existing request id
- chunk_seq: integer sequence within stream
- metrics: {token_count, decode_ms, kvcache_misses, batch_size, model_variant}
- redaction_meta: {level, rules_version, sampled_ml_scan_id?}
- trace: span(child=chunk_id) -> parent=request_root

Compatibility shim approach:
- Stream frame header includes wire_version. If wire_version==1 return legacy-frame(payload=redacted_text, meta={chunk_seq, token_count}). If wire_version==2 emit introspect-frame(payload=null, introspect_meta={metrics, trace_link, redaction_meta}).
- SDKs that speak v2 will receive richer frames; v1 clients unchanged.

Telemetry and dashboards:
- Console widget: per-session timeline UI that shows chunk tokens over time, decode latency heatmap, and redaction events (when a chunk triggered regex or ML redaction).
- Example PromQL-like queries to implement in Console backend (for engs):
  - sum by (request_id) (stream_chunk_token_count_total)
  - histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(stream_chunk_decode_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, request_id))
  - max by (request_id) (stream_chunk_max_decode_ms)

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag runtime changes behind feature:stream_chunk_introspection.
2) Launch internal-only workbench and sampling API. Enable for 10% of host accounts for two weeks.
3) Collect feedback, iterate on redaction rules, and update runbook.
4) Gradual rollout to all hosted customers with default ML-scan sampling disabled.

Testing and QA:
- Unit tests for regex scrub rules, binary compatibility for wire_version 1 frames, and span stitching correctness.
- Integration tests that simulate high-concurrency streaming to ensure metrics cardinality knobs work.
- Privacy review and internal audit required before enabling retention of sampled raw chunks.

Links and artifacts:
- Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/streaming-introspection-design (internal)
- Mockups: https://drive.google.com/mockups/stream-workbench
- Initial PoC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2354

Open questions:
- Final TTL for sampled raw chunks (current proposal: 7 days). Need legal & security sign-off.
- Sampling policy defaults: 0% for hosted, 0% for private by default, manual enable via support for enterprise.
- Should we permit customers to opt-in to store redacted chunks beyond default TTL? (security implications)

Next steps (this ticket):
- Deliver runtime instrumentation and compatibility shim (ENG deliverable).
- Create Console skeleton and wire in basic metrics (DX deliverable tracked in separate ticket).
- Schedule privacy review and include Security in the PR.
